# SigilStudio

Notes for anyone (human or agent) working in this repo.

<!-- daimon:learned:begin -->
<!-- regenerated by `daimon --learn-git`; edits here are lost -->

## Code style
- Uses TypeScript with strict typing; `tsc --noEmit` is part of the check pipeline
- React components are written in TypeScript with clear prop types
- Code follows a functional style with pure functions where possible
- Library usage: `d3-contour`, `@types/node`, React 19+, Vite

## Testing
- Tests are colocated with source code as `test_*.ts` files
- Test suite includes both unit tests and integration tests
- Tests verify behavior against real engine output, not mocks
- Test coverage includes browser verification and headless rendering
- Tests assert specific invariants like `markSet` not being patched during tour

## Commit messages
- Follow a pattern of `type: description` where type is `feat`, `fix`, or `chore`
- Messages are descriptive and explain both what changed and why
- Include verification details like "Verified in the browser" or "121 tests, 6 new"
- Reference specific files and changes in the diff

## Structure
- Source code lives in `src/` with a clear module structure
- Documentation in `docs/` including `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `USER_MANUAL.md`
- Tests are colocated with source code as `test_*.ts` files
- Build artifacts are in `dist/`, with assets under `assets/`
- Docker configuration uses `.dockerignore` to exclude unnecessary files

## Gotchas
- The render effect re-runs on every param change, but vectorization runs only when specific mark parameters change
- Object URLs are revoked immediately after decoding to prevent memory leaks
- The sheet is vectorized once per upload and cached on `params.markSet` to avoid re-computation
- The app uses a "freshUpload" ref to prevent automatic mode switching when adjusting parameters
- Thumbnail previews are data URLs, not object URLs, to survive URL revocation
<!-- daimon:learned:end -->
